title: Energy Detection for Cognitive Radio with Distributional Uncertainty and Signal Variety under Nonlinear Expectation Theory
summary: Classical energy detection (ED) methods for cognitive radio (CR) have addressed noise uncertainty as deviations in noise power and signal uncertainty as variability in signal characteristics, which use probabilistic methods and assume fixed probability distributions for both. In practical scenarios, due to the uncertainty in probability models and the significant variation of primary signals encountered by receivers across different radio technologies, wireless environments exhibit not only distributional uncertainty but also substantial signal variety.
